fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. God says it straight to Ezekiel: "But you must not mourn or weep or let your tears flow." (Ezekiel 24:16) This is one of the heavy parts of the passage. I think this one hurts.

Yes, baker. God says, "Put on your turban and strap your sandals on your feet…" (Ezekiel 24:17) A turban is a head wrap. The turban goes on his head, and the sandals go on his feet. Those are the two things God names.

I see why that one showed up, friend. But it's not what God says to Ezekiel. He says, "Put on your turban and strap your sandals on your feet…" (Ezekiel 24:17) Sackcloth and a torn robe never come up in these verses.
Right, baker. God tells Ezekiel, "do not cover your lips or eat the bread of mourners." (Ezekiel 24:17) The bread of mourners is off the table for him. I think that's a hard word to carry.

Yes, baker. God says, "I am about to desecrate My sanctuary, the pride of your power, the desire of your eyes, and the delight of your soul." (Ezekiel 24:21) Notice He calls it "My sanctuary." It's His, and He calls it the desire of their eyes.
That's right, baker. God says, "And the sons and daughters you left behind will fall by the sword." (Ezekiel 24:21) This is a heavy line. I think it's okay to sit with that for a second.
That's right, baker. Ezekiel says, "Your turbans will remain on your heads and your sandals on your feet." (Ezekiel 24:23) They stay on. The people will do just what Ezekiel did.

Good thinking, friend, but that's not what the sign is for. God says, "When this happens, you will know that I am the Lord GOD." (Ezekiel 24:24) The sign points to God, not to Ezekiel. What they will know is about Him.

I see why you'd pick that, baker, but God doesn't say that here. He says, "…you will know that I am the Lord GOD." (Ezekiel 24:24) Babylon never comes up in this verse. What they will know is about Him.
